items.title: New Thanet Local Plan: scoping consultation
items.plain: Closed. Was the first step in deciding where new homes, jobs and roads go in Thanet for the next 15 years, and which places stay protected.
items.detail: Launched 24 August 2026. Closed as scheduled at 5pm on 9 October 2026; the portal now reads "This consultation has now closed." Early scoping stage of the new Local Plan, which also asked for development site suggestions and local heritage landmarks. Reported as the start of a blueprint for around 15,000 homes. Drop-in session: Friday 2 October, 9am to 4.30pm, Cecil Street, Margate. The council aims to send the final plan to a government inspector by March 2028 and adopt it in February 2029. No outcome or summary-of-responses report has been published yet. The council's Local Plan Committee was reportedly due to meet on 11 November 2026 to consider the consultation outcomes and next steps, per the council's own Instagram account; checked again on 13 October 2026, no meeting by that name appears anywhere in the council's published October-November 2026 committee calendar (which lists Cabinet on 3 November, Standards Committee on 5 November, Constitutional Review Committee on 10 November, Overview and Scrutiny Panel on 17 November and Planning Committee on 18 November, but no 11 November entry and no committee called 'Local Plan Committee'). Treat the 11 November date as unconfirmed, not established fact. Checked again on 19 October 2026: two further, independent sources now point to the same date — the council's own Instagram account states the Local Plan Committee 'is due to meet on 11 November 2026 to report on outcomes from the consultation and prepare the Local Plan', and the planning consultancy Chelgate Local, writing on 13 September 2026, says representations will be reported to the Local Plan Committee in November 2026 before submission to the Secretary of State. The council's own published committee calendar still could not be checked for a meeting under that name this cycle (a page-rendering limitation, not a negative finding). Treat 11 November 2026 as likely, now corroborated by two independent sources, but still not confirmed against the council's own calendar. Checked again on 20 October 2026: still no meeting called 'Local Plan Committee' appears on the council's published meetings list on thanet.moderngov.co.uk, and the council's own consultation portal (thanetcouncilplan.inconsult.uk) now blocks automated access, so it could not be checked this cycle either. The 11 November 2026 date remains likely but still unconfirmed against the council's own calendar.
items.how: The consultation has closed.

items.title: Dog control rules for beaches and open spaces (PSPO renewal)
items.time: public comment closed 6:59pm, 9 Oct 2026; now in a council review and report-writing phase on Your Voice Thanet, running to 6:59pm, 26 Nov 2026
items.plain: A three-year renewal of the dog rules. New: no dogs on the beach and mudflats all year between Cold Harbour and Plum Pudding at Birchington, and dogs on leads on the northern sea wall there. Public comment has closed; officers are now writing up a report for councillors.
items.detail: Cabinet approved going to consultation on 27 August 2026. Replaces the order agreed in October 2023. Existing measures continue: clearing up after dogs, leads on promenades and in sensitive places such as Pegwell Bay, seasonal dog exclusion on selected beaches from 1 May to 30 September (a Blue Flag condition), and putting a dog on a lead when an officer asks. The new Birchington restriction follows evidence of significant bird disturbance from Bird Wise East Kent. Local news on 28 September 2026 reported some dog walkers unhappy with the Birchington proposal. Public comment closed as scheduled at 6:59pm on 9 October 2026; Your Voice Thanet now shows the project in a post-consultation review and report-preparation phase, running 12 October 2026 to 26 November 2026. No summary of responses or Cabinet report has been published yet. Checked again on 15 October 2026: no Cabinet or Overview and Scrutiny report has been published yet, consistent with the 26 November 2026 review-phase end date; the project's own Your Voice Thanet page returned a platform error on direct fetch this cycle, so the review-phase dates above rely on the 12 October check, not an independent re-read. Confirmed directly on Your Voice Thanet on 19 October 2026: the project is in its fourth phase, 'Post consultation review', running from 19:00 on 12 October 2026 to 18:59 on 26 November 2026, with 580 people having taken part. The final wording will go to the Overview and Scrutiny Panel and then to Cabinet for approval; no Cabinet report has been published yet. Independently corroborated on 26 October 2026 via the council's own moderngov decision record (issue 50546, first published 20 July 2026, status ‘Recommendations Approved (subject to call-in)’): it lists the Cabinet decision to consult on 27 August 2026, an Overview and Scrutiny Panel on 17 November 2026 and a further Cabinet on 26 November 2026 — consistent with the review-phase end date above, though Your Voice Thanet itself could not be independently re-read this cycle.
items.how: Public comment has closed; no action is currently open. Watch for the Overview and Scrutiny Panel and Cabinet report, expected once the review phase ends.

items.title: National Grid Sea Link: decision due (cable and converter station at Minster Marshes)
items.body: National Grid via Planning Inspectorate / Energy Secretary
items.time: statutory decision deadline is 3 months from the 30 Jul 2026 recommendation (about 30 Oct 2026); the Secretary of State opened a further consultation to interested parties on 22 Sep 2026, closing 22 Oct 2026, leaving little room before the statutory date; an MP report on 1 Sep 2026 said a decision was expected in November
items.plain: The public examination is over and no new comments can be made. The Examining Authority sent its recommendation to the Energy Secretary on 30 July 2026, who has three months to decide (about 30 October, though recent reporting points to November). After that, there are six weeks to challenge the decision in court.
items.detail: A £1.1bn subsea cable from Suffolk to Pegwell Bay with a converter station near Richborough. Examination ran 5 November 2025 to 5 May 2026. If approved, Kent works could run to 2031, seven days a week (7am to 7pm weekdays, 7am to 5pm weekends and bank holidays), with a peak Kent workforce of about 241. Kent Wildlife Trust says 13.6 hectares of habitat at Minster Marshes would be lost. National Grid has begun preparatory archaeological survey works across 7.24 hectares at Minster Marshes ahead of any decision; on 1 September 2026 MP Sir Roger Gale asked the Prime Minister to intervene, calling this premature. The Secretary of State requested further information on 28 August 2026 and then opened a further consultation limited to interested parties on 22 September 2026, closing 22 October 2026 — a new procedural step. The Planning Inspectorate's project page was checked again directly on 8 October 2026: the project is now formally shown at the Decision stage, the target completion date is still about 30 October 2026, no decision has been published, and no statement extending the statutory deadline has been found. Re-confirmed again by live fetch on 13 October 2026: the project remains explicitly at the Decision stage, the page still states 'This project is at the decision stage. The date set for this to be completed is 30 October 2026', and the 'What happens after the decision is made' stage is still marked 'Not started' with no decision published. The 'Latest update' has now moved on to 9 October 2026: the Secretary of State issued a third request for further information to the Applicant, with a response deadline of 23:59 on 16 October 2026, and accepted a late response to an earlier information request from the Crown Estate. This is further procedural activity, not a sign the 30 October target has moved, but it leaves very little time between the 16 October information deadline and the roughly 30 October decision date. Checked again on 14 October 2026: unchanged — still explicitly at the Decision stage, target completion still about 30 October 2026, no decision published. Neither the 16 October 2026 information-request deadline nor the Secretary of State's parallel consultation to interested parties (opened 22 September 2026, closing 22 October 2026) has passed yet, and no news coverage of a decision has been found. Checked again on 15 October 2026 by reading the Planning Inspectorate project page directly: unchanged in substance — still at the Decision stage with target completion of 30 October 2026, no decision published, and the 'What happens after the decision is made' stage still 'Not started'. The 16 October information-request deadline and the 22 October interested-parties consultation deadline are both now within days. No new theisleofthanetnews.com or kentonline.co.uk coverage of a decision was found. Checked again on 19 October 2026 by reading the Planning Inspectorate project page directly: the 'Latest update' box is still dated 9 October 2026, unchanged, and confirms the Secretary of State's third information request to the Applicant had a response deadline of 23:59 on 16 October 2026 (now passed, with no outcome published) and that the all-interested-parties consultation opened 22 September 2026 remains open until 23:59 on 22 October 2026. The project remains explicitly at the Decision stage with target completion still 30 October 2026; the 'What happens after the decision is made' stage is still marked 'Not started'. National Grid's own Sea Link project page corroborates a decision 'expected by 30 October 2026'. No decision has been published and no news coverage of one was found. Separately, Ofgem ran its own 'Sea Link: project assessment' consultation on network-charging questions, open 1 to 29 September 2026 — a different, now-closed regulatory process, not the planning decision tracked here. Checked again on 20 October 2026: unchanged — National Grid's own Sea Link page and theisleofthanetnews.com's coverage both continue to point to a decision expected around 30 October 2026, no decision has been published, and no further procedural update was found. The Secretary of State's consultation to interested parties, opened 22 September 2026, closed as scheduled on 22 October 2026. Checked again on 26 October 2026: the roughly 30 October 2026 target decision date is now four days away. This cycle's fetch of the Planning Inspectorate project page returned an inconsistent, apparently stale result (describing a pre-application stage and a 2025 submission date that do not match the project's known history), so its exact current stage could not be independently reconfirmed today; National Grid's own project pages were similarly inconsistent between two different URLs. No decision has been found in any news search. The last independently confirmed facts remain the 19-20 October 2026 checks: Decision stage, target completion about 30 October 2026, nothing published.
items.how: Only people already registered as interested parties could submit, including in the 22 September to 22 October 2026 consultation round. Watch the Planning Inspectorate page for the decision.

items.title: Kent and Medway councils reorganisation: decision withdrawn, on hold
items.time: on hold since 7 September 2026; no new date
items.plain: On 16 July 2026 the government chose four new councils for Kent and Medway, with Thanet, Canterbury and Dover merging into one East Kent council in April 2028. On 7 September ministers withdrew that decision and paused the process while they review it after new legal advice. Thanet District Council stays as it is for now.
items.detail: The pause covers Kent and Medway and 13 other areas (Kent and Medway's decision was paused, not formally withdrawn like four of the others). Councils were told to stop work on the new councils. Kent County Council leader Cllr Linden Kemkaran said in reporting from around 28 to 29 September 2026 that KCC would send a pre-action protocol letter to the Secretary of State 'in the coming days', ahead of a legal deadline of about mid-October 2026 (three months from the 16 July 2026 decision) to challenge that original announcement. The Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government responded that it was 'reviewing the local government reorganisation programme' and would 'move quickly to complete this work'. KCC's reorganisation preparation costs so far are reported at about £1m, with no confirmation of government reimbursement. A Local Government Chronicle report dated 5 October 2026 confirmed the letter had still not been sent, quoting the council's position that it 'will send a pre-action protocol letter to the Secretary of State in the coming days'; the same report said some other affected councils (Amber Valley, Lancashire, and Leicestershire districts jointly) have already taken protective legal steps of their own (Lancashire's letter sent 1 October 2026, per the same report). As of 9 October 2026, no source confirms Kent's letter has been sent, that judicial review has been filed, or that government has given a fuller response; KCC leader Cllr Linden Kemkaran is quoted in the same 5 October 2026 Local Government Chronicle report still saying the council intends to send a pre-action protocol letter 'in the coming days', and the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government's standing position (reviewing the programme and aiming to 'move quickly to complete this work') is also unchanged. Checked again on 12 and 13 October 2026: the government's own local-government-reorganisation-policy-and-programme-updates collection on gov.uk is still dated 'last updated 7 September 2026' with no newer entry; KCC's Devolution Committee and Cabinet report packs for 8 September and 1 October 2026 make no mention of a pre-action letter or judicial review, and no source confirms the letter has now been sent. A Kent County Council news item dated 12 October 2026, headlined around the council 'stepping up' its push for answers, could not be fully read this cycle, so its content is not relied on here pending independent confirmation. A single low-credibility blog post claiming a judicial review had been filed could not be loaded or independently verified and is not relied on here. A Local Government Lawyer report dated 23 September 2026 added some precision: it quoted KCC leader Cllr Linden Kemkaran telling a 17 September 2026 council meeting that she was 'considering a legal challenge' to the original 16 July 2026 decision, on the grounds that Kent and Medway's decision was paused rather than formally withdrawn like four other areas, and noting that any judicial review 'must be brought promptly and in any event within three months' of that decision — implying a deadline around mid-October 2026. Checked again on 14 October 2026: no source yet confirms a pre-action protocol letter has actually been sent or that judicial review proceedings have been issued, and the 12 October 2026 council news item still could not be read in full this cycle either. Significant development, 14 October 2026: the Local Government Chronicle, in a story headlined on the scale of LGR legal challenges nationally, reported that the three-month judicial review deadline for the 16 July 2026 decisions falls on 16 October 2026 (i.e. the next day), and quoted KCC leader Cllr Linden Kemkaran saying the council had 'taken steps' to protect its legal position — looser wording than a confirmed pre-action protocol letter having been sent. The same report said at least 10 of 19 affected two-tier areas, including Kent, have now taken some form of 'protective' legal action, and that a government-wide update on the LGR review was expected the following day (i.e. around 15 October 2026). Checked again on 15 October 2026: the gov.uk local-government-reorganisation-policy-and-programme-updates collection is still dated 'last updated 7 September 2026', so no government update had yet been published there as of this check, despite the Local Government Chronicle's report that one was expected. No source yet confirms a pre-action protocol letter has been sent or that judicial review has been filed, and the 16 October 2026 deadline referenced above is now imminent — worth checking again right after that date. Confirmed update, 19 October 2026: Kent County Council's own news site (12 October 2026) now states plainly that the council 'is proceeding with a legal challenge over the Government's decision on local government reorganisation in Kent', after letters sent in July, twice in August and in September went unanswered; leader Cllr Linden Kemkaran is quoted: 'I made it clear at the time of writing in September that if we did not receive a satisfactory explanation, I would consider taking the appropriate legal steps. That's exactly what we're now doing... The matter is now with the Government's legal department and the Court.' LocalGov (13 October 2026) corroborates this and reports KCC's own Green group leader, Cllr Mark Hood, called the action 'bonkers', warning of its cost and the risk of a second legal challenge if the government later reverses course. It would be inappropriate to comment further at this stage.' items.title: Manston Airport: airspace change consultation
items.body: RiverOak Strategic Partners (RSP) / Civil Aviation Authority
items.time: consultation closed 22 June 2026; CAA decision on new flight paths still pending, no timeline announced
items.plain: The Civil Aviation Authority still has to approve new flight paths before the airport could reopen, which is projected for 2029. As of late September 2026, RSP has not announced when it will submit the formal Airspace Change Proposal to the CAA.
items.detail: Two flight-path designs were put forward. About 14,000 air traffic movements a year (roughly 38 a day) were assumed. Ramsgate Town Council said aircraft would routinely overfly dense housing at 230 to 900 feet and asked for at least 1,500 feet. The next step is for RSP to publish a 'you said, we did' response to the consultation and refine the design before submitting it to the CAA; no date for that submission, or for a CAA decision, has been announced.
items.how: The consultation has closed. Watch for RSP's response document and the CAA's decision. Checked again directly on 8, 9, 12, 13 and 14 October 2026: RiverOak Strategic Partners' own airspace-procedures page confirms the Airspace Change Proposal remains at Stage 3 (public consultation closed 22 June 2026) and that a Consultation Response document 'will be produced and submitted to the CAA' — it has not yet been submitted, and no CAA decision has been announced. (A CAA-wide update to its general Airspace Change Process took effect 1 October 2026, but this is a process-wide change, not a Manston-specific decision.) Update, 12 October 2026: the CAA's own airspace-change portal has published a Standard Letter for Manston (ref ACP-2018-75, dated 15 September 2026, published to the portal 1 October 2026) explaining that under the new Air Navigation Guidance 2026 and CAP1616 version 6 (effective 1 October 2026), RSP may continue Manston's proposal under the older CAP1616 version 5.1 process, provided it submits its proposal to the CAA for a decision by 31 July 2031. This sets a long-stop submission deadline; it is not a flight-path decision, and RSP's Consultation Response document has still not been submitted to the CAA. RSP's own page, re-read on 14 October 2026, also says it expects to complete the whole seven-stage CAA process by 2028 — a further indication of how much is still to come, not a change to the long-stop deadline above. Checked again on 15 October 2026: RSP's airspace-procedures page is unchanged — still states a Consultation Response document 'will be produced and submitted to the CAA' with no dated update since the consultation closed, and no news of a Manston CAA/airspace development was found. items.title: Pierremont depot and park, Broadstairs: funding and remarketing going to Cabinet; park transfer postponed
items.body: Thanet District Council / Broadstairs & St Peter's Town Council
items.time: Overview and Scrutiny Panel met 20 October 2026; its outcome is not yet published. Cabinet decides the £400,000 funding and the depot remarketing on 4 November 2026 as planned; the separate park-transfer decision has been postponed to a future meeting (confirmed 20 October 2026)
items.plain: The buyer of the former depot next to Pierremont Park withdrew in August. The council's plan to spend £400,000 on park improvements and re-market the separate depot site for sale still goes to Cabinet on 4 November. A separate plan to transfer Pierremont Park itself to Broadstairs & St Peter's Town Council has been postponed to a future meeting, to allow more time to work up the detail.
items.detail: The 2,000-plus signature petition to stop the depot sale was debated in March 2026. The Overview and Scrutiny meeting on the call-in, planned for 25 August, was cancelled, and the agreed buyer for the depot withdrew on 24 August 2026. Local news (theisleofthanetnews.com, 12 October 2026) reports the council will propose transferring Pierremont Park itself to Broadstairs & St Peter's Town Council at market value, permanently restricted to public-park use, alongside £400,000 of Pride in Place Impact Fund money for a fountain, flowerbeds and inclusive play equipment. The former depot site, which is separate from the park, would be re-marketed for freehold sale by private treaty, going to public auction if unsold within six weeks. The Overview and Scrutiny Panel considers the proposal on 20 October 2026 and Cabinet is due to decide on 4 November 2026; no report had been published on the council's own site for either meeting as of 13 October 2026. Checked again directly on 14 October 2026: still no agenda or report published for the 20 October Overview and Scrutiny Panel meeting; no further local-news follow-up to the 12 October report was found this cycle. Checked again on 15 October 2026: unchanged — still no agenda published for the 20 October Overview and Scrutiny Panel meeting, which is now five days away; a KentOnline report on 15 October 2026 about a separate £10.7m Jackey Bakers Recreation Ground scheme is an unrelated project and does not affect the Pierremont timeline. Significant update, checked 19 October 2026: the council's own press release (thanet.gov.uk, published 12 October, updated 15 October 2026) states that the Pierremont Park transfer-to-town-council decision was postponed and pulled from both the 20 October Overview and Scrutiny Panel and the 4 November Cabinet agenda, 'to allow [the council and Broadstairs & St Peter's Town Council] to work up the proposal in more detail', and that only the £400,000 Pride in Place funding for the park and the depot re-marketing remain on track for those dates. However, the Overview and Scrutiny Panel's own published agenda for 20 October 2026 (confirmed live on 19 October, via thanet.moderngov.co.uk) still lists and sets out in full detail an item 26/082 'Pierremont Park Asset Transfer', recommending transfer of the park to Broadstairs & St Peter's Town Council at market value, retained as public parkland in perpetuity — directly conflicting with the council's own postponement announcement. The same agenda's depot item, 26/078, also describes a bidding process dated to July 2026, which predates the buyer's withdrawal in August 2026, suggesting the published document may not be the current, final version. This dashboard treats the council's own press statement as the more authoritative, current position — that the park-transfer decision has been postponed — but flagged the conflicting agenda text for a human to check once the meeting had happened or the Cabinet agenda for 4 November was published. No Full Council meeting has taken place since 24 September 2026, so no Full Council 'petitions' item has been checked in this window. Resolved, checked again 20 October 2026: a theisleofthanetnews.com report dated 16 October 2026 ('Cabinet discussion of transfer of Pierremont Park to town council postponed for further details') independently confirms the council's own account — the park-transfer item was pulled so the council and Broadstairs & St Peter's Town Council can work up the proposal in more detail, and it 'will now be discussed at a future meeting'; the £400,000 Pride in Place funding and the depot remarketing remain on track for the Overview and Scrutiny Panel and the 4 November Cabinet, as originally planned. This resolves the 19 October conflict in favour of the postponement. What the Overview and Scrutiny Panel itself discussed or recommended on 20 October could not be confirmed this cycle — no minutes, outcome report or further news coverage of that meeting had been published as of 20 October 2026; worth checking again once they appear. Checked again on 26 October 2026: still no minutes, outcome report or further news coverage of the 20 October Overview and Scrutiny Panel meeting has been found. The 4 November 2026 Cabinet date is unchanged.
items.how: No consultation is open. Watch the Overview and Scrutiny Panel report (20 October) and the Cabinet decision (4 November 2026) on thanet.moderngov.co.uk.

items.detail: An earlier consultation ran 10 March to 30 April 2026. petitions.outcome: Rejected by Parliament's petitions committee on 6 October 2022.

petitions.title: Reopen the Port of Ramsgate with a direct ferry to Belgium
petitions.outcome: Rejected by Parliament's petitions committee on 1 August 2022.

petitions.title: Hold a public meeting on the future of Margate Winter Gardens
petitions.outcome: About 2,000 signatures at submission (2,416 reported in the news). Full Council referred it to Cabinet on 14 July 2022; the report back was noted on 8 December 2022. The theatre closed in August 2022.

petitions.title: Reconsider Kent Film Foundation's bid for the Granville Theatre, Ramsgate
petitions.outcome: About 1,600 signatures in under 24 hours after the council rejected the charity's bid. The theatre was sold in October 2022 for £125,000 to Westwood One Ltd, not to Kent Film Foundation.

petitions.title: Create a town council for Margate
petitions.outcome: Reached 1,000 signatures of support in November 2021; more were needed at the time. The ask was resolved years later: Full Council voted on 18 June 2026 to create a new Margate Town Council, run by a shadow council of existing ward councillors until its first elections on 6 May 2027.

petitions.title: Repair and reopen the Ramsgate and Broadstairs seafront lifts
petitions.outcome: Presented to Full Council on 3 June 2021 and referred to Cabinet. The report back was noted at Full Council on 24 February 2022.

petitions.title: Keep the Uncle Mack memorial plaque at Viking Bay, Broadstairs
petitions.outcome: Council e-petition, ran 2 July to 2 September 2020.

petitions.title: Replant protected trees felled at Park Avenue Woodland, Broadstairs, and keep it as open space
petitions.outcome: Council e-petition, ran 20 May to 19 August 2020. More than 40 trees under Tree Preservation Orders were felled in early March 2020. At Full Council on 25 February 2021 the council said it would contest the appeal lodged against its action.

petitions.title: Bigger and more frequent bins along the Thanet coastline
petitions.outcome: Council e-petition, ran 26 June to 19 August 2020.

petitions.title: Adequate toilets and waste facilities at Thanet beaches
petitions.outcome: Council e-petition, ran 26 May to 18 June 2020. Cabinet noted the concerns and said toilet facilities serving the beaches would be reviewed.

petitions.title: Postpone the seasonal dog restrictions on Thanet beaches for a month
petitions.outcome: Council e-petition, ran 18 April to 18 June 2020.

petitions.title: Extend or remove expiry dates on residents' one-day visitor parking permits
petitions.outcome: Council e-petition, ran 27 March to 19 May 2020.

petitions.title: Let the free community sauna stay on Margate Sands until April 2020
petitions.outcome: Council e-petition, ran 14 to 16 January 2020.

watch: Sea Link on the Planning Inspectorate site
Thanet District Council meetings and agendas
watch_note: No charity or non-profit consultation was found open on 26 October 2026, after checking Kent Wildlife Trust, RSPB, Bird Wise East Kent, Thanet Coast Project, Southern Water, the Environment Agency and Natural England again. Each is either silent, running something unrelated (a photo competition, a citizen-science survey), or campaigning on a consultation run by another body (chiefly Sea Link or Kent County Council's Mineral Sites Plan), not running one of its own. This gap has now persisted across sixteen refresh cycles (25 Sep, 28 Sep, 2 Oct, 5 Oct, 6 Oct, 7 Oct, 8 Oct, 9 Oct, 12 Oct, 13 Oct, 14 Oct, 15 Oct, 16 Oct, 19 Oct, 20 Oct, 26 Oct 2026). A Thanet District Council survey of local voluntary, community and social enterprise groups for its UK Shared Prosperity Fund work was also found this cycle, but it is a stale 2023 page with a long-passed deadline, not a current consultation, so it has not been added. These organisations remain the likeliest to run one. Canterbury City Council's charity-run "Right to Grow" pilot with the community group Revival (Salt Marsh Lane, Whitstable) closed 13 July 2026, with further rounds flagged for autumn and winter 2026 — worth watching for a reopening, though that is in Canterbury district, not Thanet.
empty_charity: No charity or non-profit consultation was found open on 26 October 2026. Try the places to watch.
